title: Degreewise bijectivity of the canonical odd quotient map
statement: Let $A$, $K$, $S_a$, $e_a$, the zero positive column hypothesis, and the explicit filtration be as in [lem-pc-derived-total-filtration-stable]. Suppose every $S_a$ is short exact. Let $q_j:(S_j).X_3[j]\to\operatorname{coker}(s_{2j+1})$ be the canonical descent of the full-column cochain map of [lem-pc-derived-total-filtration-odd-quotient-map]. For every $j\in\mathbf N$ and $k\in\mathbf Z$, its degree component $q_j^k$ is a bijection of the underlying $A$-modules. No degreewise splitting, free endpoint, or vanishing endpoint differential is required.

proof.text: Use the total coproduct universal property to project onto column -j, then compose with e_j inverse and (S_j).g. This projection kills every earlier full column and every lower-column generator, using (S_j).f composed with (S_j).g equal to zero for column j. The supremum definition of the stage implies that the projection vanishes on stage 2j+1.

Restrict the projection to stage 2j+2 and descend through the evaluated categorical cokernel. Evaluation preserves cokernels. Its composite with the full-column quotient map is (S_j).g in degree k+j. The defining factorization of q_j and degreewise epimorphy of (S_j).g imply that the projection is a left inverse of q_j^k. Thus q_j^k is injective.

Show from the supremum that stage 2j+2 is contained in stage 2j+1 plus the range of full column j. Lift a quotient vector through the degreewise surjective cokernel projection, split that lift into the two summands, and kill the first. Transport the remaining column vector by e_j inverse. It maps to the original quotient vector under the full-column quotient map. The factorization through (S_j).g gives a preimage under q_j^k, proving surjectivity. All steps are proved in Lean.
